The partnership

How we work together

Many accounting and tax firms do not maintain a dedicated in-house R&D credit specialist. Provenance provides that capability when you need it: handling the R&D credit study while your firm retains the client relationship and the tax return.

You receive a completed Form 6765 package supported by client-specific analysis and documentation, ready to incorporate into your existing tax process. Provenance integrates into your workflow without disrupting it, giving your firm another way to deliver value to clients.

The engagement

What a study involves

01

Eligibility review

A structured review of what your client designs, builds, and improves, to determine what qualifies for the credit and to what extent.

02

Technical interviews

Conversations with the engineers, developers, and product staff who did the work, to establish and document the qualifying activity.

03

Quantification

Qualified research expense analysis and the qualifying-percentage determination, with contemporaneous documentation assembled to support both the position and the figures.

04

Form 6765

Preparation of the credit and the return form, including the Section G business-component detail.

05

Documentation package

Technical narratives, qualified research expense workpapers, and a methodology memorandum.

06

Audit support

Responses to IRS Information Document Requests, the substantiation an examiner asks for, and representation before the IRS.

Why now

Why this is worth your attention now

Tax year 2026

Form 6765 Section G, the business-component breakdown of qualified spend, becomes mandatory for the 2026 tax year. Filers at or below $1.5M in qualified research expenses and $50M in gross receipts are exempt.

Examination

R&D credit claims continue to face IRS scrutiny. Strong, well-supported documentation can make all the difference when a claim is examined.

Unclaimed

Business owners rarely think of their own work as research, so qualifying activity in your client base can go unnoticed year after year, and the credit along with it.

What sets us apart

What sets Provenance apart

From the high-volume firms
High-volume R&D credit models can prioritize speed and standardization over depth of analysis. Provenance takes a more deliberate approach, with client-specific analysis, continuity throughout the engagement, and credit positions supported by the client’s specific fact patterns.
From software and self-serve tools
Software can calculate a credit. But it cannot replace the judgment, documentation, and professional accountability needed to support the position in an examination. We deliver a study run by a skilled practitioner, with the substantiation to stand behind it.
From handling it in-house
Building R&D credit capability in-house takes time and specialized experience. Provenance brings that expertise without the overhead of building a dedicated function internally.

You get the study done efficiently, the work delivered clearly, and a partner who fits into the way your firm already works.

Specialization

The experience behind every study

Sean Wang
Principal, R&D Tax Credit Advisory

Every Provenance engagement is led directly by Sean Wang, an Enrolled Agent with deep experience advising businesses on the federal R&D tax credit from initial assessment through documentation, calculation, and IRS examination support.

His work has spanned a broad range of industries, including software and hardware development, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, financial institutions, hospitality, industrial engineering and manufacturing, consumer goods, and government contractors developing technology for public-sector applications. That cross-industry experience helps Provenance quickly understand how different businesses innovate, where qualifying activities may exist, and how to build a well-supported credit position around the facts.

As an Enrolled Agent, Sean is authorized to represent taxpayers before the IRS. When examination support is needed, clients benefit from continuity with the same practitioner who understands the technical work, the calculations, and the documentation behind the credit.
